criterion: F37 bounded human swim presentation witness
scope: One trainer, two fixture crossings, Low Compatibility at actual 1280x720. Still frames and native-pixel crop sequences only.

review_basis.rubric: Unchanged ACCEPTANCE section 4 full Bars A/B; owner Tidewake dune direction.
review_basis.comparison: Previously inspected matched trainer-A and trainer-B captures; same retained judge. B2 frame-index.json was read only for image-to-PNG/time metadata. Game source and capture-report.json were not inspected.
review_basis.sample_limit: The supplied sample span is 30.0167 simulation seconds. JPG sheets do not establish continuous 30-second playback, interpolation, cadence or frame rate. Not every raw frame was inspected.

preference.reason: B2 communicates alternating arm activity and forward swimming intent more clearly than A's upright moving-standing appearance and B's repeated raised-V arms. Identity and recovered dry standing are ties. Relative preference does not close the absolute visual bar.

body_identity_and_gameplay_distance_visi.scope: Shown trainer only; no four-body or close facial-quality certification.
body_identity_and_gameplay_distance_visi.reason: Hair, teal jacket, pack, dark trousers and boots preserve the reference character identity and remain recognizable in ordinary native views.

sampled_reach_pull_recovery_intent.scope: Bounded intent recognition in the supplied sequence, not commercial motion quality or continuous-playback acceptance.
sampled_reach_pull_recovery_intent.reason: The denser cycle shows one arm leading, lowering beside the torso and exchanging with the other arm, with alternating knee activity. This reads as an attempted crawl cycle rather than the repeated two-arms-up shape. Underwater pull/contact is less clear than above-water recovery, and there is little visible wake/splash coupling.

lower_limb_silhouette.reason: A straight translucent submerged leg pair remains visible while differently posed solid bent/extended legs move above it. The combined image gives a mismatched or doubled lower-limb silhouette at gameplay distance. Translucent submerged legs also occur in A and B; images do not establish their cause or which change introduced the mismatch.

restored_dry_standing.reason: Dry exit shows a recognizable standing body with both boots visible and no apparent residual swim pose. Immediate shallow-water exit is not the same as a fully exposed dry endpoint.

entry_exit_continuity.reason: Before/after samples now show the standing-to-swimming and swimming-to-standing endpoints in both directions. They still cannot establish smooth interpolation or continuous foot contact. The c1 exit toast obscures part of the lower body in the immediate after frame.
evidence: transition-4.jpg c2 human_exit_before moving 35.67 s and human_exit_after moving 35.78 s

persistent_body_geometry_penetration.reason: No definite persistent trainer/terrain or trainer/creature mesh penetration is diagnosed in the inspected stands. Water intersection alone is expected for swimming. This sample does not cover the enumerated pose, slope and camera matrix, and cannot certify absence of clipping throughout motion.

combined_human_motion_presentation.reason: Readable stroke intent and restored standing do not overcome the persistent mismatched lower-limb presentation, weak water-contact feedback and unreviewed transition/playback continuity.

water_surface_readability.scope: Displayed Low daytime surface around the trainer only.
water_surface_readability.reason: Cyan surface and shallow/deep separation remain readable; no visible surface hole surrounds the trainer.

water_full_presentation.reason: The mismatched submerged silhouette and little convincing stroke-to-water wake/splash relationship weaken integration. This is not a full water, shoreline or mount matrix.

grounds_paths_vegetation_rocks.reason: Broad warm sand and sparse upright grass follow the owner dune direction. Repeated sand ripples, smooth berm shapes and simplified tree/rock materials remain below the reference's natural variation and commercial integration. Sparse dunes are not themselves a density defect.

architecture_props_pickups.reason: The fixture lacks sufficient ordinary/detail views for this domain.

creatures.reason: The large shore creature is recognizable, with coarse surface treatment and angular form visible in the close encounter. Its body/shadow dominates part of the return view without proving trainer penetration. This is not a creature fight or full pose review.

sky_light_atmosphere.reason: Daylight preserves useful trainer contrast, but flat horizon haze, sharply graphic cloud treatment and limited depth/material atmosphere fall below the reference and full Bar B.

Low_UI_readability.scope: Displayed labels and values at native 1280x720 only, not a physical handheld certification.
Low_UI_readability.reason: Quest text, menu labels, controller glyphs and the swim-lesson toast are readable. Health/food contrast is weak, the largely uniform minimap provides little coastline context, and the toast obscures part of the trainer in the immediate exit view.

full_bar.reason: Improved sampled stroke intent is a bounded component finding. The human lower-limb mismatch and water/world/material/atmosphere limitations remain, and the full region and hero-subject matrices are absent. The owner-settled full bars are not lowered to close this fixture.

still_open: Close continuous shoreline entry/exit and foot-contact proof
Full enumerated poses, slopes, cameras and persistent-clipping matrix
Other three human bodies and four-body matrix
Full principal-region and hero-subject matrix including a real fight
Earned ordinary-route proof for all F37#2 mandatory water routes
Physical device/controller readability and performance proof
acceptance_limit: No whole-F37#2, earned-campaign, device, High/Medium or four-body acceptance is claimed. No game source, report or index was edited; this verdict.json is the only written artifact.
